relation: two contracts under the corpus name "spanning_tree", sharing only the name. LABELLED simple graphs (canonical GTBase.spanning_trees.fg_spanning_tree, B18): X167.x167_spanning_tree and X168.x168_spanning_tree (T \subset fg_edges G /\ is_tree [set: fg_labelled_sgraph T]: a set of valid edges of G whose labelled graph on the WHOLE vertex carrier of G, isolated vertices included, is an upstream tree) are fg_spanning_tree T by conversion; the subset guard stays part of the contract (the labelled-graph constructor drops only malformed members and keeps every two-element member, so host non-edges are excluded by the guard alone), host connectivity follows, and the conventions are derived from upstream is_tree: the empty edge set spans 'K_0 (vacuously) and 'K_1, the single edge spans 'K_2, the triangle's full edge set, any disconnected host and any host with at least two vertices one of which is isolated are rejected. MULTIGRAPH edge carriers (canonical Cycle.foundations.spanning_trees.spanning_tree_edge_set over Cycle.foundations.connectivity and path_subgraphs, B19): Cycle.U6.spanning_tree (spanning_connected T /\ acyclic T: an undirected uwalk inside T between every two HOST vertices, and no circuit inside T) is spanning_tree_edge_set T by conversion, the conjunction of the all-host-vertex restricted walk spanning_connected_edge_set and the public acyclic_edge_set; U6's unchanged supports spanning_connected and acyclic are frozen as copies but not migrated. Conventions: the empty host and the empty carrier are accepted vacuously, one vertex with the empty carrier is accepted beside an unselected loop, a single non-loop edge spans its two-vertex host in either reference orientation, a third isolated vertex defeats spanning connectivity although the carrier stays connected on its incident support, and a selected loop, parallel pair or digon is rejected; no loopless, simplicity, nonempty-carrier or nonempty-host guard is added. No equivalence between the two representations is stated. summary: Family B18 (labelled spanning trees of finite simple graphs). The helpers `X167.x167_spanning_tree` and `X168.x168_spanning_tree` (`T \subset fg_edges G /\ is_tree [set: fg_labelled_sgraph T]`) now unfold to the new public `GTBase.spanning_trees.fg_spanning_tree T`, the same body over `GTBase.finite_graph` and upstream `is_tree`, by conversion. Contract: `T` is a set of valid edges of `G` (the subset guard is kept: the labelled-graph constructor retains every two-element member, including host nonedges, and ignores members that are not pairs; the subset guard rejects host nonedges) whose labelled graph on the WHOLE vertex carrier of `G`, isolated vertices included, is a tree (unique irredundant paths and connected). Conventions derived from upstream `is_tree`, never added as guards: the empty edge set spans `'K_0` (vacuously) and `'K_1`; the single edge spans `'K_2`; the triangle's full edge set, one edge of the triangle (a vertex is missed), two isolated vertices and any set containing a singleton are rejected. No nonempty guard, edge-count characterisation or validity repair is introduced.
